# `m.stocks.filings.insider_holdings`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Each company's insiders and the shares each one holds now, one row per insider.

```python
m.stocks.filings.insider_holdings(symbols=None, *, issuer_cik=None, owner_cik=None, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| Time range | `start` and `end` are sent as `last_filing_date.gte` and `last_filing_date.lte` |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `IssuerCik`, `OwnerCik` and `Symbol` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | none |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Tickers whose issuers' insiders to return; None, the default, for every issuer. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `issuer_cik` | The issuing company's SEC CIK, as text with its leading zeros, or a sequence of them; None, the default, for every issuer. |  |
| `owner_cik` | The insider's SEC CIK, or a sequence of them, to list every company one person is an insider of; None, the default, for every insider. |  |
| `start` | The earliest latest-filing date (`LastFilingDate`); an insider who has not filed since is left out. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last latest-filing date. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | The field to sort by, such as `"shares_owned"`; the default is the most recent latest-filing date first. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Unused today: the arguments above reserve every endpoint parameter, so any key raises `ValueError`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The ticker the request named that the row lists in `Tickers`: a row that lists several of the named tickers appears once for each, so an article about AAPL and MSFT read for both is listed under each. A request that named one ticker gives it to every row. Null when the call named no ticker, and on a row that lists none of a request's named tickers. | REST |
| `FilingCount` | long | Number of Form 3, 4, and 5 filings by the owner for this issuer. | REST |
| `FirstFilingDate` | String | Date of the owner's first Form 3, 4, or 5 filing for this issuer (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). Filings begin in 2003. | REST |
| `IssuerCik` | String | SEC Central Index Key of the issuer company (10 digits, zero-padded). | REST |
| `IssuerName` | String | Name of the issuer company as reported in the most recent filing. | REST |
| `LastFilingDate` | String | Date of the owner's most recent Form 3, 4, or 5 filing for this issuer (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). | REST |
| `OfficerTitle` | String | Title of the officer in the most recent filing, if the reporting owner is an officer. | REST |
| `OldestPositionDate` | String | Earliest as_of_date among the summed positions (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). A date far behind last_filing_date means at least one position has not been restated recently and may be stale. | REST |
| `OwnerCik` | String | SEC Central Index Key of the reporting owner (10 digits, zero-padded). Stable across issuers and years; use it to follow a person through the Form 3, 4, and 5 endpoints. | REST |
| `OwnerName` | String | Name of the reporting owner (individual or entity) as reported in the most recent filing. | REST |
| `OwnershipPct` | double | shares_owned as a percentage of the issuer's shares outstanding (largest share class) as of last_filing_date. Absent when shares outstanding is not available for the issuer. | REST |
| `PositionCount` | long | Number of positions summed into shares_owned: one for direct holdings plus one per indirect vehicle. | REST |
| `Roles` | String[] | Relationships of the reporting owner to the issuer in the most recent filing. Possible values: director, officer, ten_percent_owner, other. | REST |
| `SharesOwned` | double | Shares of the issuer's non-derivative securities the owner holds: the sum of the latest reported balance of each position (direct, and each indirect vehicle) across their Form 3, 4, and 5 filings. As filed, not adjusted for splits. Unexercised options and other derivative securities are not included. Absent when the owner has never reported a share balance. | REST |
| `SharesOwnedDirect` | double | Shares held directly, in the owner's own name. | REST |
| `SharesOwnedIndirect` | double | Shares held indirectly through trusts, LLCs, family members, and other vehicles. | REST |
| `Tickers` | String[] | Ticker symbols of the issuer as of the owner's most recent filing. Multiple symbols may indicate different share classes. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
